sources.title: Vector networks
sources.author: Figma
read_sections: Create vector networks using the Pen tool
sources.read_content: P selects Pen. Click places points, dragging controls curves, returning to a point closes a path, Escape leaves it open. Open paths can use different endpoint caps.
sources.adopted_detail: Closed filled paths for each custom white glyph; separate open curves for orange loops and short accents.
sources.limits: No Chinese glyph construction or SHANYEJI process. No automatic distress reconstruction.

sources.title: Edit vector layers
sources.author: Figma
read_sections: Create curved paths with bézier handles
Erase parts of vector paths or shapes
Select points and paths with the Lasso tool
Edit multiple points using bounding boxes
Round the corners of a shape
sources.read_content: Enter exposes points and paths. Bend adds Bézier handles with independent or mirrored controls. Cut splits geometry. Eraser removes regions and adds editable points. Paint changes closed-region fills.
sources.adopted_detail: Keep sharp mountain corners, refine orange-curve handles, and cut irregular voids or edges with editable geometry.
sources.limits: Text Outline was not verified here. Dense distressed grain would be laborious as individual points. Article describes editing tools rather than a specific lettering design.

sources.title: Boolean operations
sources.author: Figma
sources.read_content: Union merges outer geometry; Subtract removes overlap from the bottom object; Intersect retains shared regions; Exclude removes shared regions. Select two or more supported layers. Boolean groups preserve modifiable children.
sources.adopted_detail: Union stroke pieces within a glyph. Subtract triangular counters and distressed voids. Keep the orange path independent to retain overlap order.
sources.limits: Geometry operations do not infer glyph anatomy, distress distribution, or the original designer's actual construction method.
